title: The Ninth Pillar: Choosing Righteous Companions and Avoiding Bad Company
reference_info: Abd al-Razzaq ibn Abd al-Muhsin al-Badr, 'Ashr Raka'iz fi Tarbiyat al-Abna' (Ten Pillars in Raising Children), in Arabic, p. 28

(٢٦٢٨) « ﻪ ﺤﻴﺤﺻ» ﰲ ﻢﻠﺴﻣو ،(٥٥٣٤) « ﻪ ﺤﻴﺤﺻ» ﰲ يرﺎﺨﺒﻟا ﻪﺟﺮﺧأ ( ١) . (٩٢٧) « ﺔ ﺤﻴﺤﺼﻟا ﺔﻠﺴﻠﺴﻟا» : ﺮﻈﻧاو ،(٤٨٣٣) « ﻦ ﻨﺴﻟا» ﰲ دوادﻮﺑأ ﻪﺟﺮﺧأ ( ٢) 
text_simplified: Companionship has a profound impact on a child's righteousness or corruption. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The example of a righteous companion and a bad companion is like that of the seller of musk and the blacksmith's bellows: as for the seller of musk, either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will find a pleasant scent from him; and as for the blacksmith's bellows, either he will burn your clothes, or you will find a foul smell from him" (Sahih Muslim 2628). It is therefore obligatory to keep children away from bad companions who lead them into deviation.
